text:
jen: Heads up — ALB started deregistering ~30 targets from us-west-2 edge pool at 11:02 UTC. Readiness probes are 503 only when checks come from ALB health-check ranges. Rolling back envoy change did not help.

matt: Seen similar. Any recent change to egress/SNAT or client-ip ACLs? :thinking:

jen: Nothing obvious in deploy history besides the client-ip-check filter we enabled last week. Locally curling the pod readiness endpoint -> 200. From a node (which SNATs) -> 503.

tara: Could be kube-proxy/conntrack interaction + SNAT causing healthcheck source IPs to look different and trigger the ACL. @raj can you check conntrack and iptables?

raj: On it, pulling conntrack and iptables.

infra-bot: Alert: target-group/usw2-edge-pool unhealthy count increased to 30 (+18 in 5m)

sam: Reminder of the path: ALB healthcheck -> nodePort -> kube-proxy -> pod. If SNAT rewrites source IPs and our filter expects ALB source, anyone mismatch could be rejected.

jen: Posting the envoy deny log where filter rejects healthcheck traffic with 503.

```
[2025-04-18T11:02:12Z] [debug] filter: client-ip-check: denied request from 100.64.5.12 -> 127.0.0.1:8080, reason=unknown-client
[2025-04-18T11:02:12Z] upstream: backend returned 503, path=/healthz/readiness
```

matt: Are these nodes using iptables mode or ipvs for kube-proxy? Could change conntrack semantics.

raj: Nodes are iptables. Conntrack shows many entries from ALB ranges. Running quick check:

```
$ conntrack -L | grep 100.64. | wc -l
4200
```

tara: 4200 is huge for a single node pool. That suggests conntrack table getting full / evicting entries intermittently. Evictions can break established flows and cause weird failures for healthchecks.

sam: Also worth checking ephemeral port exhaustion / node-local ENI port assignments. If nodes rotate egress IPs because of port scarcity, ALB healthchecks can appear from different source IPs and our strict client-ip filter will reject them.

jen: As a quick mitigation I'm rolling a canary to disable the client-ip-check filter on edge namespace to see if targets re-register.

deploy-bot: Rollout started: disable-filter edge/client-ip-check v2 -> v3 by jen (canary: 10%)

matt: Canary node shows immediate recovery — targets re-registered.

raj: I'm increasing conntrack max on the pool and adding a cron to prune stale entries. Also requested infra to increase node ENI ephemeral port quota for pool nodes.

tara: Follow-ups: 1) add explicit ALB health-check allowlist before client-IP gating, 2) emit metric for conntrack table usage and node ephemeral-port saturation, 3) add test simulating heavy health-check + egress churn.

jen: Confirming: after the temporary disable + conntrack tweaks, target group healthy count is back to normal. Filing postmortem ticket INFRA-4251.

sam: Thanks all — great cross-team response. :thumbsup:
